title: Unified OTel exporter for inference KPIs and Prometheus compatibility
creator: Anika Shah
description: Build a lightweight, production-ready OpenTelemetry exporter and metric shaping layer for the inference runtime that emits both Prometheus-compatible metrics (for existing dashboards and Alertmanager rules) and custom inference KPIs (tokens_per_sec, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_cpu_ms, tail_latency_ms). The exporter will live in the runtime process as well as a standalone sidecar option for Private deployments. Goals: 1) preserve low-latency path, 2) avoid high-cardinality explosion by enforcing stable label sets and cardinality limits, 3) support histogram buckets aligned to our latency SLOs, 4) provide a remote_write-compatible output for Cortex/Thanos and an OTLP/OTLP-http path for traces to Tempo/OTel Collector.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits OTel metrics for core KPIs with stable labels: model_name, model_version, route, deployment_type, customer_tier
Prometheus scrape-compatible metrics are available on /metrics for hosted runtime and sidecar; existing Grafana dashboards render without panel changes
Latency histograms use agreed buckets (0-5ms,5-10ms,10-25ms,25-50ms,50-100ms,100-250ms,250-1000ms,>1000ms) and 50th/95th/99th percentiles match sampling tests
Cardinality controls reject additional custom labels beyond whitelist and log a single telemetry event per minute when exceeded
OTLP traces include correlation_id and model_version and can be joined to metrics in Tempo for tail-latency investigations
Exporter passes load regression tests: <2% added p50 latency at 95th percentile production load with 8k RPS benchmark
updates: 2026-02-24: Spike complete — validated OTel SDK (Go runtime) can export both OTLP and Prometheus concurrently without duplication. Prototype added a metrics shaping layer in-memory.

2026-03-02: Decision: implement exporter as thin in-process module + optional sidecar to support Private air-gapped installs. Sidecar will handle remote_write to Cortex when direct remote write not available.
2026-03-04: Trade-off: we will enforce a label whitelist and automatic cardinality bucketing instead of full dynamic label support to protect Prometheus TSDB and rollout velocity.
2026-03-06: Benchmarks: prototype increased p50 by 0.9% and p99 by 1.8% under synthetic KV cache heavy workload (8k RPS) — acceptable. Detailed numbers in perf-run-2026-03-06 link.
2026-03-09: PR opened for runtime changes and OTel exporter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2187
2026-03-10: Integration test added for histogram buckets and label-whitelist enforcement. Next: add automated migration for existing dashboards to use new metric names and update Alertmanager rules.
